    name="consumer_mv",
    comment="Silver consumer view with cleaned data",
    table_properties={"quality": "silver"}
)
def consumer_mv():
    # Read from bronze view as a streaming source
    df = spark.readStream.table(bronze_table)
    # Trim whitespace from string columns
    string_cols = ["name", "gender", "email", "phone", "address", "city", "state", "country"]
    for c in string_cols:
        df = df.withColumn(c, trim(col(c)))
    # Phone: keep digits only
    df = df.withColumn("phone", regexp_replace(col("phone"), r"\D", ""))
    # Nullify phone if less than 10 digits
    df = df.withColumn("phone", when(length(col("phone")) < 10, None).otherwise(col("phone")))
    # Convert registration_date to date type
    df = df.withColumn("registration_date", to_date(col("registration_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
    return df

import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, trim, regexp_replace, when, length, to_date
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.getActiveSession()
catalog = spark.conf.get("catalog")
target_schema = spark.conf.get("target_schema")  # silver target schema, e.g., consumer_silver
# Derive bronze schema from silver target
bronze_schema = target_schema.replace("_silver", "_bronze")
bronze_table = f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.consumer_mv"

@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_consumer_id", "consumer_id IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.table(
    name="consumer_mv",
    comment="Silver consumer view with cleaned data",
    table_properties={"quality": "silver"},
    schema="""
        consumer_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
        name STRING,
        age INT,
        gender STRING,
        email STRING,
        phone STRING,
        address STRING,
        city STRING,
        state STRING,
        country STRING,
        registration_date DATE,
        is_active BOOLEAN
    """
)
def consumer_mv():
    # Read from bronze table as a batch source
    df = spark.read.table(bronze_table)
    # Trim whitespace from string columns
    string_cols = ["name", "gender", "email", "phone", "address", "city", "state", "country"]
    for c in string_cols:
        df = df.withColumn(c, trim(col(c)))
    # Phone: keep digits only
    df = df.withColumn("phone", regexp_replace(col("phone"), r"\D", ""))
    # Nullify phone if less than 10 digits
    df = df.withColumn("phone", when(length(col("phone")) < 10, None).otherwise(col("phone")))
    # Convert registration_date to date type
    df = df.withColumn("registration_date", to_date(col("registration_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
    return df
